title: A gate on a content item whose touched article's path names a secrets word is classed by its question, not secrets by the path
goal: gate add on an item whose touches name a kb article such as kb/public/auth/shamir-secret-sharing.md classes a design question (which anchor rows to keep) by its own wording, not secrets because the touch path holds 'secret', so a wording or ledger choice on an article about secrets is not made blocking and operator-only; a gate that names a secret value or a credential file stays secrets. In SP-6ukmjucf, ST-hojn6yjd's g1 was classed secrets from its touch path alone and its landing waited on the operator.

run:
import sys
sys.path.insert(0,'_tools')
import bl_authority as a
item=dict(touches=['kb/public/auth/shamir-secret-sharing.md'])
g=dict(id='g1',question='Which anchor rows of the article does the fix keep: the old rows or the reworded ones?',options=['keep the old rows','replace them with the reworded rows'])
bad=dict(id='g2',question='Should the worker read the credential file .env to fetch the value?',options=['read it','leave it'])
c1,c2=a.derived_class(item,g),a.derived_class(item,bad)
print('wording choice on a secrets-named article:',c1,'| credential file gate:',c2)
sys.exit(0 if c1=='design' and c2=='secrets' else 1)

notes: SP-6ukmjucf retrospective finding (2026-10-14), parked as a draft by the orchestrating session acting for the operator.
